claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is a random solid solution with high configurational entropy.
The random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution has significant lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch.
Induced short-range order can produce ordered B2-like HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
Thermal annealing or controlled cooling can reproduce the short-range-order pathways generated by Monte Carlo simulations.
Short-range order can form below the bulk transition temperature for long-range ordering or precipitation.
The relevant high-frequency phonon regime is above 10 THz.
The B2-like HfTi and TiZr clusters form a percolating network.
The ordered clusters locally relax lattice strain relative to the random configuration.
Transitioning from a random structure to B2-like order reduces the local variance in atomic size and bonding environments.
Reduced lattice distortion suppresses the scattering of high-frequency phonons.
Percolating ordered clusters create continuous pathways for phonon transport.
The continuous transport pathways override the phonon-scattering effects associated with chemical disorder.
Ordering shifts the high-frequency phonon density of states to higher frequencies or energies.
Hardening of the high-frequency phonon spectrum increases phonon group velocities.
Percolating B2-like chemical order produces a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random-alloy baseline.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has low thermal conductivity because random lattice distortion strongly scatters phonons.
The conductivity increase occurs only after the short-range-order clusters form a percolating network.
If the ordered clusters remain isolated, lattice thermal conductivity decreases rather than increases.
If ordering produces large-scale precipitates that act as grain boundaries, lattice thermal conductivity decreases.
A percolating-cluster sample showing lower conductivity than the random alloy, or phonon-DOS softening rather than hardening, would falsify the hypothesis.
